title: Waiver Add Lift (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Waiver Add Lift. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points, in-season). WHAT IT MEASURES: For a free agent, the net gain in your STARTING-lineup points across the remaining season if you add him and drop your worst rosterable player. INPUTS (general): free-agent projections, your current roster, weeks remaining. HOW TO READ IT: A positive lift that clears a noise threshold = a real add; a tiny or negative lift = the waiver buzz is hype, your roster is already better. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Ranking who to actually claim; beats picking up the player with the gaudiest raw projection, because what matters is the gain to YOUR starting lineup, not his points in a vacuum. COMMON MISTAKE: Chasing big names whose points don't crack your starting lineup. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Optimal Drop (Marginal-Contribution Drop)
body: CONCEPT: Optimal Drop. SPORT: Fantasy Football (in-season). WHAT IT MEASURES: Which player on your roster you can cut for the LEAST cost -- the one whose absence subtracts the least from your starting-lineup value over the remaining season. HOW TO READ IT: The best drop isn't your lowest-projected player overall; it's the one your optimal lineup leans on least once byes and positional depth are accounted for. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Making room for an add; beats dropping by raw projection or gut feel, which can cut a player your lineup quietly needs on a bye week. COMMON MISTAKE: Dropping a useful bye-week fill-in because his season total looks small. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Starting-Lineup Value (Lineup Optimizer)
body: CONCEPT: Starting-Lineup Value. SPORT: Fantasy Football. WHAT IT MEASURES: The points your BEST legal starting lineup is projected to score each week (slots filled to maximize total, not just legality), summed over the weeks you care about. INPUTS (general): roster, weekly projections, league slot rules. HOW TO READ IT: It's the yardstick every add, drop, trade, and start/sit is measured against -- a move is good only if it raises this number. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: The engine under waiver and trade decisions; beats counting bench points, which never score. COMMON MISTAKE: Valuing roster depth that never reaches the starting lineup. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Streaming Candidacy (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Streaming Candidacy. SPORT: Fantasy Football (in-season). WHAT IT MEASURES: Whether a position is better STREAMED -- rotating a fresh free agent in each week by matchup -- than rostered as a fixed starter. Highest at high week-to-week-variance positions (QB, TE, K, DEF). HOW TO READ IT: If the weekly ceiling of the best available streamer rivals your rostered player, don't tie up a roster spot -- stream the matchup. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Deciding whether to roster a fixed QB/TE/K/DEF or churn them; beats rostering a mediocre fixed starter at a streamable position. COMMON MISTAKE: Holding a low-end fixed starter where a matchup-based stream would outscore him. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: FAAB Bid Sizing (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: FAAB Bid Sizing. SPORT: Fantasy Football (in-season, Free-Agent Acquisition Budget). WHAT IT MEASURES: How much of your remaining waiver budget to bid on an add, scaled by the add's lift to your starting lineup and the budget you have left. HOW TO READ IT: A high-lift add early in the season justifies a big bid; a marginal add late justifies a token bid -- spend in proportion to value and runway. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Setting a FAAB number; beats flat bidding or emptying the budget on hype, which leaves you broke when a real difference-maker hits the wire. COMMON MISTAKE: Overspending early on a streamer-tier add and having nothing left for a league-winner. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Injury Replacement (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Injury Replacement. SPORT: Fantasy Football (in-season). WHAT IT MEASURES: The add/drop decision when a starter is ruled out -- it runs on the SAME machinery as any waiver move (add lift, optimal drop, streaming, starting-lineup value), just triggered by the hole the injury opens. INPUTS (general): the injured player's lost starting value, available free agents, weeks the hole persists. HOW TO READ IT: Compare the best available replacement's lift against holding/stashing the injured player (an IR slot, if you have one, costs you nothing to keep him); short-term holes lean streaming, season-enders lean a real add + drop. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: 'My TE just got ruled out -- who do I grab?'; beats panic-adding the most-hyped name without checking it actually clears your lineup. COMMON MISTAKE: Dropping the injured starter outright when an IR stash keeps him for free, or overpaying for a one-week patch on a multi-week hole. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Schedule-Adjusted Add Value (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Schedule-Adjusted Add Value. SPORT: Fantasy Football (in-season). WHAT IT MEASURES: How an add's value shifts once you weight his REMAINING schedule -- soft upcoming matchups raise a streamer/flex add, a brutal stretch lowers it. HOW TO READ IT: Two adds with the same raw projection aren't equal if one faces bottom defenses down the stretch and the other faces top units; the easier slate is worth more, especially in the fantasy playoff weeks. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Choosing between similar adds, and timing claims for the playoff push; beats raw season projection, which ignores when and against whom the points come. COMMON MISTAKE: Ignoring playoff-week matchups when adding a streamer for the stretch run. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).
